title: Parked-action loading and rescind flow for icon & compact buttons
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Users sometimes trigger quick successive actions on compact/icon-only buttons (e.g., 'retry', 'dismiss', 'save draft') which the runtime may park when upstream latency spikes. This ticket defines a resilient UX for parked (queued) actions that clarifies in-flight state, provides a clear cancel/rescind affordance, and preserves theming and a11y parity across themes and density scales. The goal is to reduce accidental duplicate submits, make cancellation discoverable for keyboard/screen-reader users, and avoid layout jank when toggling from icon-only to loading state.
context_and_problem: We have recurring regressions where icon-only buttons flip to a full-width spinner or puff layout when a request is queued. This causes layout shift and loss of affordance on small toolbar clusters. Recent incidents: ENG-49210 noted doubled submits in compose toolbar; QA regressions surfaced when dark-mode tokens changed spinner tint (DES-940412). Current behaviors are inconsistent across densities (compact vs comfortable) and theme variants, and there is no accessible keyboard flow to rescind a parked action.
goals: Introduce a non-layout-shifting parked state for icon and compact buttons
Add a discoverable cancel/rescind affordance (keyboard + pointer) for queued actions
Maintain consistent spinner and icon contrast across all themes and densities
Provide animation guidelines that avoid motion-induced layout shift and meet reduced-motion preferences
Document telemetry hooks and small API contract for engineering (queuedId, canRescind)
acceptance_criteria: Icon and compact buttons show a compact parked indicator (overlay dot + subtle pulse) instead of expanding into a full spinner container
A visible cancel control appears on hover/focus (icon-sized 'x' overlay) and is reachable via keyboard (focus order includes rescind control).
Screen reader announces: 'Action queued. Press Escape to cancel.' when an action becomes parked; keyboard ESC triggers rescind API and returns the button to its pre-queued state.
No layout shift occurs when going into/out of parked state at any viewport or density; regression tests for toolbar clusters pass.
Spinner and overlay colors match tokenized tints for light/dark/high-contrast themes; automated visual diff across themes passes.
Design tokens used are documented; Engineering can implement using only existing token primitives (no new global tokens unless absolutely necessary).
Telemetry fields added to spec: queuedId (string), queuedAt (ISO), rescindInitiatedBy (user|system|timeout). Spec docs link included.
QA acceptance: keyboard-only flow, screen reader narration, and pointer cancel all validated in latest candidate build.
implementation_notes: Prefer overlay-dot + alpha pulse to indicate queued work rather than replacing the icon with a spinner
Rescind control should be an overlay button with aria-label='Cancel queued action' and tabindex=0 when visible
ESC key global mapping only triggers rescind when the button has an active parked state and is focus-visible
Avoid introducing new global tokens; use existing semantic tokens: token.surface-foreground, token.overlay-muted, token.action-accent
Keep animation duration < 160ms for state transitions; respect prefers-reduced-motion by switching to instant opacity toggles
Provide small CSS-only fallback for environments where JS fails: a data-attribute-driven visual state with no layout changes
notes_for_engineering: Engineering: you'll receive a small token mapping table in the confluence spec; if a new token is required, justify with a short note in PR.
The runtime will emit queuedId; we need a small contract for the front-end to attach a rescind call to the runtime endpoint: POST /actions/{queuedId}/rescind
Unit tests: visual regression snapshots for compact toolbar at 3 breakpoints and both themes; accessibility tests for narration and keyboard flow
